IBM.rationale: IBM shows solid fundamental health with Q1 2026 revenue up 9.5% YoY to $15.92B, strong operating cash flow of $5.17B, and improving margins (gross margin 58.4%, operating margin 15.3%). The company beat EPS estimates ($1.91 vs $1.81 expected) and raised its dividend to $1.69/quarter (3.1% yield). Software segment grew 11.3% with ARR at $24.6B, and Infrastructure surged 15.3% on mainframe demand. However, QoQ metrics show sequential deceleration (revenue -6.2%, EPS -44.6% vs Q2 2025), and the stock has declined 15.9% over the past quarter, suggesting the market has already priced in some concerns. Valuation is attractive vs history: P/E of 19.3x is near the low end of its 19-51x range over the past year, and P/B of 6.3x is at the bottom of its 6.2-10.8x range. The $11.6B Confluent acquisition adds execution risk and increased debt to $57.7B, but also expands the data streaming portfolio. Near-term catalysts include the FedRAMP authorization for 11 AI products and ongoing z17 mainframe cycle, though federal contract cancellations ($100M) and consulting revenue pressure present headwinds.
